homonyms.basis: Wikipedia's article opens with the hatnote 'This article is about the magazine. For the alternative currency, see Labour voucher.' (F18): labour notes, the labour-time currency (Owen's labour notes among them), is a distinct entity under the name, never a sense of it. T composes no other entity under the name, and no card is a homonym. Inside the archive the Epistle's apparatus has 'LABOR notes:' (#85, #1187), the notes of its LABOR voice, a string homonym of the name met only by a case-insensitive match (traversal reading.json, not admitted). The census row carries no relations and no disambiguation field. The Labor Education and Research Project is the census's other name for the entity (aka) and Wikipedia's publisher of the magazine (F8): the same organization, carried as the operator. The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the entity and are never senses of its name.

atoms.evidence: Labor Notes is an American media and organizing project
founded in 1979 by labor activist Kim Moody
it reports on rank-and-file union democracy, strikes, and independent worker-led organizing efforts.
Publishes 11 issues annually covering shop-floor strategy, union elections, and grassroots campaigns across major sectors.
Operating as a voice for the "troublemaking wing" of the labor movement
